title: First peopling of Sahul (Australia and New Guinea)
note: Child of the out-of-Africa record. Contested start: ~65 ka at Madjedbebe (Clarkson et al. 2017, Nature) versus ~48–50 ka (O'Connell et al. 2018, PNAS, PMC6112744); genomic models assume settlement by 47.5–55 ka (Malaspinas et al. 2016, PMC7617037). Cover the open-sea crossings of Wallacea (≥ 70 km legs) and the Denisovan admixture (~44 ka). Centre Aboriginal and Papuan perspectives where sourced; id year reflects the claimed early date, so revisit if the record settles nearer 50 ka.

title: Madjedbebe rock shelter
note: Mirarr country within the former Jabiluka mineral lease, surrounded by Kakadu (UQ news 20 Jul 2017). Exact coordinates not found in opened sources (only GeoNames Jabiluka Mine as proxy) — need a heritage or scholarly coordinate. Ground-edge axes, grindstones, ochre; Gundjeihmi Aboriginal Corporation agreement; dating dispute as perspectives. If importance ≥ 3 a model is required; consider importance 2 or a minimal sourced model.

title: Lida Ajer cave, Sumatra
note: Teeth excavated by Eugène Dubois 1887–1890, re-identified as H. sapiens and dated 73–63 ka (Westaway et al. 2017; full text at repository.naturalis.nl). Earliest claimed rainforest occupation by modern humans; O'Connell et al. 2018 question the teeth's provenance. Indonesian researchers (Rokus Due Awe, Indonesian Centre for Archaeology) on the team. Cave coordinates not published in the paper body — check supplementary material.

title: Tam Pà Ling cave, Laos
note: TPL 1 U-series dated 63.6 ± 6 ka, but O'Connell et al. 2018 argue the remains were redeposited into 40–50 ka sediments. Mainland Southeast Asia is under-recorded; look for the Demeter et al. papers and later re-dating of the site (open access PNAS/Nature Communications likely).

title: Denisovans
note: Archaic group known mainly from genomes; ~4% (3.3–5.0%) of Papuan and Aboriginal Australian genomes (Malaspinas et al. 2016), admixture ~44 kya. Denisova Cave (Altai, Russia — check region code), Baishiya Karst Cave (Tibetan Plateau), and the Tibetan high-altitude haplotype noted by López et al. 2015. Divergence from Neanderthals 381–473 kya per López et al. 2015 — verify against primary papers.

title: Jebel Faya, Sharjah
note: Levallois, blade and bifacial tools dated ~125–130 ka (MIS 5e), basis of the 'Jebel Faya model' of an early southern dispersal across Arabia (Groucutt et al. 2015, PMC6715448). Arabia is thin in the atlas; pair with the Nubian/'beaked' Levallois sites in Oman and the humid-phase (Green Arabia) climate record.
